question: Apply the method of differentials to estimate $\sqrt{99.8}$. Explain the effect of the negative increment on the approximation.
explanation:
Choice of variables
Let $y=\sqrt{x}$, with $x=100$ and $dx=-0.2$. The increment is negative because $99.8<100$.
Differential of the function
$$dy=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}dx$$
Substitution
At $x=100$,
$$dy=\frac{-0.2}{2\sqrt{100}}=\frac{-0.2}{20}=-0.01$$
Approximation
$$\sqrt{99.8}\approx\sqrt{100}+dy$$
$$\sqrt{99.8}\approx10-0.01=9.99$$
Sign interpretation
The negative differential reduces the value from $10$, which is consistent with $99.8$ being less than $100$.
Conclusion
Therefore, $\sqrt{99.8}\approx9.99$.

options.A: $10.01$; the negative increment increases the approximation
options.B: $9.99$; the negative increment reduces the approximation from $10$
options.C: $9.90$; the negative increment reduces the approximation from $10$
options.D: $10.00$; the negative increment produces no change
